claims: The release exact-data-2026-10-12 (published 2026-10-12T14:14:15Z, tagged at 31523f8) publishes s29-minpoly.tar.zst, 87,237,962 bytes, SHA-256 708e1b8b45894667f90a0d18b55bb35ed6079b84d33f9656976fd5cfa6f3729c: the degree-7213 polynomial p of the s(29) record side (n29_poly_q4.json), the shape-lemma parametrization n29_param_t1..t5.json, the exported system n29_system.jl, the Krawczyk box n29_krawczyk.json (radius 1e-50), the side to about 40,000 digits (n29_S0.txt), the four roots recovered algebraically (n29_q4_ref133k.txt) and the original verification logs, 201,735,244 bytes in 21 files unpacked. The release rates irreducibility, Krawczyk uniqueness and the root link (link.py at PREC=220000) rigorous, the identities in Q[x]/(p) and the contact-system consistency Monte Carlo, and leaves the packing's non-overlap at the exact point unchecked.

It publishes gradec-233.tar.zst, 238,231 bytes, SHA-256 c71633f3850eb8b06c40ba04f824e9b6262b27b7996f62f69c6ad014a4ea9fa3: n-N.contacts.json and n-N.gradec.json for the 233 configurations gradec.py certifies VALID (231 directly, 230 and 261 with GRADEC_DROPZERO=1), and the run logs of all 250, including the 17 timeouts; 15,787,809 bytes in 723 files unpacked.

The issue comment reports that the author re-ran each s(29) step from the packed files (krawczyk.py the same t* in 46 s, link.py LINKED in 9 s, verify_mod.py and contacts_mod.py passing with one prime each, irred.py the same degree patterns), prices a full replay with 12, 50 and 21 primes at about 2.5 CPU-hours, almost all in verify_mod.py, and reports that recomputing the n = 10 grade-C certificate from the committed exact forms gave an identical certificate.
